scope: Changes to Sigil SkillWorkflow and SigilCli SourceFormattingCommand/SourceFormatting/WorkspaceMutationBoundary for mechanical skill validation and multiple fmt targets; other contracts outside scope.

authority.verification: All six captured input hashes, evaluator entrypoint identity, language manifest identity, and language-pack output hashes matched their supplied digests.

coverage.assessment: No material design contradiction, consequential omission, ownership conflict, or commitment-preserving simplification was identified within the requested scope.
reviewed_commitments: Sigil SkillWorkflow logic and constraints: compatible mechanical tooling, writer check/correction/format/recheck sequence before capture, read-only evaluator commands, continued design work when mechanical validation is unavailable, preservation of diagnostic outcomes, evidence scope and revision matching, and separation from semantic and implementation judgments.

SigilCli SourceFormattingCommand: multiple file and directory targets, deduplicated selection within one configured workspace, omitted-path selection, workspace-root selection, and the distinction between configuration discovery and selected targets.

SigilCli SourceFormatting logic, constraints, and cases: deterministic workspace source ordering, combined replacement validation, selected-file mutation, read-only formatting checks, diagnostics, and exit outcomes.
SigilCli WorkspaceMutationBoundary: whole-invocation target preflight, no writes for invalid targets or unrepairable selected-source errors, and the explicit limit on rollback guarantees.
Related CLI help and formatting rationale insofar as they clarify the selected command's observable behavior.
relationships: The CLI owns target selection, workspace validation, preflight, writes, and failure reporting; SigilFormatter retains pure canonical rendering and meaning preservation.
ConfigFile and SourceSelection retain workspace and inclusion/exclusion authority. Multiple targets do not transfer that authority to paths or ordinary module files.
The authored scope is consistent with the captured user intent and plan requirements R1–R9. Compact contract wording leaves compatible implementation choices open.
omitted_scope: Unrelated root, compiler, CLI, and language contracts.
Implementation conformance, actual CLI behavior, and planned skill/documentation implementation.
Exhaustive workspace import validation or saturated coherence.

limitations: This was an independent, read-only design assessment of the identified captured bytes. No CLI validation or runtime tests were performed.
The host restriction was instructions only: filesystem writes and mutating commands were prohibited by the request, without an enforced read-only sandbox. No files were written.
Coverage is revision-bound. The caller must verify current draft, context, intent, authority, and original-path mapping before reusing this report.
Existing linked skill implementations were not evaluated for conformance to the proposed workflow; updating those implementations is later work under the supplied plan.
